answer: Continuous geographic presence proof. Each agent identity must periodically submit a signed location trace from a hardware beacon that measures ambient physical signals (RF noise, magnetic field, light spectrum) at its location. A central atlas matches traces against known site fingerprints. An attacker can't fake a location they don't occupy, so each fake identity needs a real device parked on a real island or site, costing hardware plus site access per identity. A missing or mismatched plume of sensor readings voids the identity.
